title: Height-three coefficient unimodality: bounded first investigation
objective: Investigate constructive lower-half first differences of the elementary coefficient indexed by (n-4,3,1) for every height-three natural unit interval order, retaining complete determinant sectors and exact obstructions without claiming a new theorem from finite success.
deliverables: Primary-source frontier audit, exact target, written sector derivation and unresolved novelty questions
Frozen development and held-out cases, complete raw signed states and twelve deterministic selectors
Source-bound bounded execution records with failures, resource caps and independent coloring comparisons
At most two author-critic rounds; forest-triple comparison after a certified tableau grammar obstruction
success_criteria: Every determinant permutation is retained; negative indices vanish and zero indices mean e_0=1
First-difference states have sign sgn(sigma)(-1)^epsilon and degree inv+epsilon, restricted to the lower half
An explanatory universal proof, exact coloring bridge, placeholder-free Lean checking and separate semantic review are required to claim the theorem
A new proof of established positivity alone does not satisfy the user's unresolved-theorem novelty gate
Capped cases, failed rules and unresolved disagreement are preserved rather than scored as successes
stop_conditions: Two construction proposal/review rounds, no nested agents or fleets
Per round: 600 computation seconds, 5000000 enumeration extensions, 5000000 move candidates, one enumeration process
Per case: 120 seconds; memory at most 2 GiB and artifacts at most 250 MiB
No new dependencies, installations, paid compute or external certificate rebuild
No substantial Lean work before a credible universal mathematical argument
